question.zh: 怎样在 X 上写一条有人读、读完能学会东西的技术帖或 thread?
question.en: How do you write a technical post or thread on X that people read and learn something from?

text.zh: 他的技术帖有固定的形状:开头一句话点出一个反直觉的点并承诺「读完你就懂」,正文一帖一个点、配代码图,结尾给可执行的结论;零散的帖子定期汇总成按难度排序的合集,或沉淀成文章、newsletter。
text.en: Open with a counter-intuitive point and a promise that the reader will understand it. Give each post one point and a code image. End with an actionable conclusion. Collect scattered posts into lists ordered by difficulty, articles or newsletters.

anchors.quote: I promise you'll understand them by the end of this thread.
anchors.quote_zh: 我保证,读完这个 thread 你就会懂。

title.zh: 开头:一个反直觉的点 + 一个承诺
title.en: Open with a counter-intuitive point and a promise

how.zh: 第一句话说清楚这条帖子讲什么,并制造一点张力(「看起来很疯狂」「你可能从没听说过」),紧接着承诺读者读完就能理解。读者在第一屏就知道值不值得读下去。
how.en: The first sentence says what the post is about and adds a little tension ("looks crazy", "you've probably never heard of"), then promises the reader will understand by the end. Readers know on the first screen whether it is worth continuing.

anchors.quote: But I promise by the end of this thread, you'll know how it works.
anchors.quote_zh: 但我保证,读完这个 thread 你就知道它是怎么回事。

anchors.quote: a super useful type helper you've probably never heard of
anchors.quote_zh: 一个超有用、你大概从没听说过的类型工具

title.en: One point per post, with a code image

how.zh: 每条帖子(或 thread 的每一条)只讲一个点,用一张代码截图或示意图承载细节,文字只负责说明「为什么」。2022 年他用编号的「TypeScript Tip」系列固定了这个格式,并保持工作日更新的节奏。
how.en: Each post (or each part of a thread) covers one point, with a code screenshot or diagram carrying the detail and the text only explaining why. In 2022 his numbered "TypeScript Tip" series fixed this format and kept a weekday rhythm.

anchors.quote: I've been posting an Advanced TS tip every weekday
anchors.quote_zh: 我一直在每个工作日发一条进阶 TS 技巧

title.zh: 把零散帖子汇总成有序的合集
title.en: Gather scattered posts into ordered collections

how.zh: 积累到一定数量后,发一条「合集」thread,把过去的内容按从入门到高级排好顺序——单条帖子的生命很短,合集能被反复收藏和转发。
how.en: Once enough have built up, post a collection thread that orders past content from beginner to advanced. A single post lives briefly; a collection gets bookmarked and shared again and again.

anchors.quote: Here's every piece of free content I've put out over the past 6 months, in order from beginner to wizard-level.
anchors.quote_zh: 这是我过去 6 个月发布的所有免费内容,按从入门到高手排好了顺序。

title.zh: 把值得长期保留的内容搬出信息流
title.en: Move content worth keeping out of the feed

how.zh: 平台算法会逼人降低质量;值得长期查阅的内容写成面向搜索的文章,或放进自己掌控的 newsletter。
how.en: Platform algorithms push people to lower quality; content worth looking up later becomes search-oriented articles or goes into a newsletter you control.

anchors.quote: I have to lower the quality of what I post to fit the algorithms.
anchors.quote_zh: 我不得不降低发帖质量来迎合算法。

title.zh: 本站示例:一条 thread 的骨架
title.en: Our example: the skeleton of a thread

body.zh:
1/ 反直觉的点 + 承诺:「T[number] 看起来很疯狂,读完你就懂。」
2/ 最小例子(代码图)
3/ 心智模型(一句话)
4/ 实际用途(代码图)
5/ 结论 + 链接到长文或合集
body.en:
1/ Counter-intuitive point + promise: "T[number] looks crazy; by the end you'll get it."
2/ Smallest example (code image)
3/ Mental model (one sentence)
4/ Real use (code image)
5/ Conclusion + link to the long article or collection

title.zh: 泛型 thread(2023,他互动最高的 TS 帖之一)
title.en: The generics thread (2023, one of his most engaged TS posts)

text.zh: 为了迎合算法降低内容质量——他 2024 年因此转向站外 newsletter。
text.en: Lowering quality to please the algorithm; in 2024 this pushed him to an off-platform newsletter.

text.zh: 只发不汇总:单条技巧很快被信息流淹没,读者找不到学习顺序。
text.en: Posting without collecting: single tips sink fast in the feed and readers can't find a learning order.

stance.zh: 编号的「TypeScript Tip」系列,工作日更新;发按难度排序的合集 thread。
stance.en: The numbered "TypeScript Tip" series on weekdays; collection threads ordered by difficulty.

stance.zh: thread 数量进入高峰;同时写面向搜索的文章;2024-03 认为算法逼人降质,转向 newsletter。
stance.en: Thread output peaks alongside search-oriented articles. In March 2024 he says the algorithm pushes quality down and turns to a newsletter.

stance.zh: thread 明显减少,帖子转向 AI 编程工作流的短帖和清单,很少再谈写帖方法本身。
stance.en: Threads become much less frequent. Posts shift to short notes and checklists about AI coding workflows, with little discussion of how to write posts.
